## Definitions

- [statement] Variational's documented public API is a market-statistics REST endpoint (GET /metadata/v2/stats, 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP). An unofficial, reverse-engineered TypeScript client on GitHub says Variational publishes no trading API and no API keys, and warns its API can change without notice. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/technical-documentation/api · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/Magicianhax/variational-trading-api/blob/main/README.md
- [statement] Variational's documented public API is a market-statistics endpoint, GET /metadata/v2/stats, limited to 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP and 1000 requests per minute globally, with HTTP 429 and a retry_after_seconds field on excess. An unofficial, reverse-engineered TypeScript client states that Variational publishes no trading API and no API keys. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/technical-documentation/api · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.variational.io/llms.txt, https://github.com/Magicianhax/variational-trading-api/blob/main/README.md
- [statement] Variational's documented API is a market-statistics REST endpoint (GET /metadata/v2/stats; 10 requests per 10 seconds per IP, 1000 requests per minute global, HTTP 429 with retry_after_seconds). Its docs roadmap lists 'Enable API trading', a November 2026 Business Wire press release says its roadmap for the remainder of 2026 includes launching a trading API, and Bankless reported that on Nov. 4th the API would go to a small group of alpha testers ahead of a public launch this month. An unofficial, reverse-engineered TypeScript client exists and says Variational publishes no trading API and no API keys and that its API can change without notice. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/technical-documentation/api · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.variational.io/getting-started/roadmap, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116481769/en/Variational-Raises-%24110M-Series-B-at-%241.5B-Valuation-To-Scale-On-Chain-Access-To-Global-Markets, https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public, https://github.com/Magicianhax/variational-trading-api/blob/main/README.md

## Structure and components

- [statement] Variational Omni charges no trading fees: its docs say 'There are no trading fees on Omni', plus a flat $0.1 fee per deposit/withdraw and liquidations at ask price + 0.5% (short) or bid price - 0.5% (long); Omni generates revenue by capturing the spread, and the Variational Protocol receives a cut of that spread revenue. A Business Wire press release says the OLP structure 'allows Omni to charge no trading fees', and CoinGecko ('Zero trading fees') and CoinLaunch ('0% trading fees') also list zero trading fees. CoinGecko's Variational section is marked as brought to you by Variational, so it is not independent. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.variational.io/omni/trading/fees · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261116481769/en/Variational-Raises-%24110M-Series-B-at-%241.5B-Valuation-To-Scale-On-Chain-Access-To-Global-Markets, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/best-perp-dexes-and-on-chain-trading-platforms, https://coinlaunch.space/blog/perp-dex-list-best-perpetual-trading-platforms/

## How it works

- [statement] Extended documents a REST API throttled by IP address (default 1,000 requests/minute, a 429 status code when exceeded, higher tiers on request), a WebSockets API, a Python SDK, and RFQ markets where market makers pick up user orders. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.docs.extended.exchange/
- [statement] EdgeX offers a V2 API with public endpoints (market data, metadata and funding rates; no authentication required), private endpoints that need a signature-based authentication mechanism, WebSocket APIs, and official SDKs including a Python SDK repo under the edgex-Tech GitHub organisation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/api-v2 · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/edgex-Tech/edgex-python-sdk
- [statement] Aster's recommended V3 futures API signs requests with an EIP-712 signature made with an API wallet ('signer'); the nonce uses microsecond precision and is valid only within a window of 60 seconds before and after server time, and each agent address maintains only the most recent 100 nonces. An optional nonceWindow (valid range 1 – 60000 milliseconds) causes a request the sequencer has not processed by nonce + nonceWindow to be rejected, returning code -4227. New V1 API key creation is no longer supported from March 25, 2026, but existing API keys continue to work. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation, https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs
- [statement] BULK's trading API uses Ed25519 signatures for state-mutating operations (official bulk-keychain library for Node, browser, Python and Rust). Public mainnet limits per client IP are 5 requests/second sustained with a 150-request burst for API requests and 5 actions/second with a 64-action burst for order actions through /api/v1/order; WebSocket allows 32 actions/second per connection (96-action burst) and 15 concurrent connections per client IP. BULK applies a 25 millisecond speed bump to transactions that may take liquidity, while transactions containing only provably maker-only orders proceed immediately; the docs call the speed bump a temporary launch mechanism limited to the first 90–120 days. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.bulk.trade/api-reference/introduction · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.bulk.trade/api-reference/rate-limits, https://docs.bulk.trade/architecture/taker-speed-bump

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Aster's published perp fee schedule lists a 0.04% taker fee for Crypto-General pairs (varies by VIP tier), a 0.1% taker fee for Group B alt pairs, and a 1.25 bps taker fee for RWA pairs (effective September 7, 2026); all maker fees are 0 bps. Aster is therefore zero-fee on the maker side only. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/perpetuals/fees-and-specs/fees · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://www.coingecko.com/learn/best-perp-dexes-and-on-chain-trading-platforms
- [statement] Aster's API returns HTTP 429 when rate limits (RAW_REQUEST, REQUEST_WEIGHT, ORDER) are broken, and repeatedly ignoring 429s without backing off triggers an automated IP ban (HTTP 418). The docs steer clients to WebSocket streams for market data to reduce REST weight. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs
- [statement] edgeX's VIP fee page lists a base ('Regular User') tier of 0.040% maker / 0.045% taker for perpetuals, falling to 0.015% maker / 0.020% taker at VIP 6, and edgeX docs say fees are tiered on a rolling 30-day trader volume with sub-account volume aggregated with the main account. edgeX is not a zero-fee venue at base tier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://pro.edgex.exchange/vip · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/trading/trading-fees
- [statement] GRVT's published perps schedule pays a maker rebate at every tier (-0.0001% at tier 1 up to -0.003% at tier 9, $1,000,000,000 of 30-day volume) and charges 0.045% taker at tier 1 down to 0.024%, so takers pay a positive fee at every tier. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/9614699-how-does-grvt-s-fee-model-work · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program
- [statement] GRVT's MM program page states a 25ms speedbump for major trading pairs and a 50ms speedbump for altcoins to minimize toxic flow. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-26) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program
- [statement] Pacifica's base tier (tier 1) is 0.015% maker and 0.040% taker; maker fee reaches 0.000% only at VIP 1 (above $100,000,000 of 30-day rolling volume). Pacifica is near-zero only for large makers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/trading-fees · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://castlelabs.io/research/perp-dex-rankings/pacifica
- [statement] Variational Omni charges no trading fees; traders pay the spread. Its OLP market maker is the counterparty to all trades on Omni, and the protocol currently keeps 20% of spreads paid to OLP, a share the docs say is still being tested and subject to change. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://docs.variational.io/omni/the-omni-liquidity-provider-olp · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public, https://castlelabs.io/research/reports/mapping-the-perpetual-trading-ecosystem
- [statement] Base-tier taker fees on the venues read are Extended 0.025%, Aster 0.04%, GRVT 0.0450%, Pacifica 0.040% and EdgeX 0.045%. Maker fees are zero or a rebate at Extended (0.000%), Aster and GRVT (-0.0001%), but not at Pacifica (0.015%) or EdgeX (0.040%). (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/trading/perpetuals/fees-and-specs/fees · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.extended.exchange/extended-resources/trading/trading-fees-and-rebates, https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/9614699-how-does-grvt-s-fee-model-work, https://docs.pacifica.fi/trading-on-pacifica/trading-fees, https://pro.edgex.exchange/vip
- [statement] Polymarket Perps schedules, for November 25, 2026, an increase in base-tier (below $1M of 30-day volume) taker fees from 0.0400% to 0.0500% and maker fees from 0.0125% to 0.0200%, and a liquidation fee increase from 0.50% to 1.00% of liquidated notional. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.polymarket.com/perps/fee-and-liquidity-reward-changes-november-2026
- [statement] A trading firm's analysis says Lighter, Aster, edgeX and Paradex each lost 60-95% of their volume as rewards wound down. It is a single source from a firm that says it invested heavily in Hyperliquid infrastructure, and it notes nobody outside those teams can compare these venues in users because per-user activity never touches a public ledger. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-29) — https://myshterious.substack.com/p/hyperliquid-is-still-sticky-after

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] GRVT's 9-level perps schedule pays makers a rebate at every level (-0.0001% at level 1, reaching -0.003% at level 9, $1,000,000,000 of 30-day volume) while takers pay 0.045% at level 1 falling to 0.024%. Its MM program adds larger rebates by maker share (0.005% Bronze at 2.5% or more, up to 0.011% Diamond at 10% or more), with perks including an RPI whitelist (Gold) and a rate-limit increase (Diamond). Resting orders are paid; takers still pay. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/9614699-how-does-grvt-s-fee-model-work · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program, https://www.coingecko.com/learn/best-perp-dexes-and-on-chain-trading-platforms, https://castlelabs.io/research/perp-dex-rankings
- [statement] Aster V3 time-in-force values include GTX (Good Till Crossing, Post Only) and HIDDEN, and POST /fapi/v3/chase places a BBO-pegged GTX limit order that automatically re-pegs to the best bid/ask as the market moves until it fills or the market moves beyond maxChaseOffset from the original BBO. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation
- [statement] GRVT's rate limits are based on the main account ID and shared across all sub-accounts. At every tier (1 to 9) Create is 260 and Cancel is 2600 per (/10sec); GetOrder rises from 50 at tier 1 to 650 at tier 9; concurrent WebSocket streams rise from 30 at tier 1 to 110 at tier 9; and open orders are checked against account/instrument with a limit of 20 at tier 1 rising to 100 at tier 9. The GRVT MM program lists a rate limit increase as a Diamond-category benefit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/9636566-what-are-the-rate-limitations-on-grvt · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program
- [statement] Decibel's REST API and WebSocket streams are served from Aptos Labs' node API at https://api.mainnet.aptoslabs.com/decibel (WebSocket wss://api.mainnet.aptoslabs.com/decibel/ws), with requests authenticated by an Authorization Bearer node API key header. Hummingbot's decibel_perpetual connector supports LIMIT, LIMIT_MAKER and MARKET order types in one-way position mode, and a Hummingbot bounty (#8028) was opened to add a Decibel Perpetual connector. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.decibel.trade/quickstart/api-reference · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://hummingbot.org/exchanges/decibel/, https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8028
- [statement] GRVT's MM program page states a 25ms speedbump for major trading pairs and a 50ms speedbump for altcoins to minimize toxic flow. BULK holds taker-capable transactions (market, GTC or IOC limit, modify, stop or take-profit) for 25 ms, while ALO limit orders go immediately. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.bulk.trade/architecture/taker-speed-bump
- [statement] DefiLlama stopped showing Aster's perp volume on 5 October 2025 after its founder found it tracked Binance's almost one for one, and has counted it again since 15 October 2025, holding volume to what open interest supports. AirdropAlert's Aster review likewise says DefiLlama delisted then relisted Aster while warning the numbers could not be independently verified. Castle Labs ranks Aster by open interest ($1.09B, second of 42 venues by DefiLlama's count on 22 November 2026). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://castlelabs.io/research/perp-dex-rankings/aster · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://airdropalert.com/blogs/aster-review/
- [statement] On November 10, 2026 (UTC), an attacker exploited an accounting flaw in Arcus Perps on Robinhood Chain that allowed transfers between subaccounts to artificially inflate an account's recorded balance and withdrew 2,234,391 USDG; an additional $3 million in withdrawal requests was blocked by the bridge's rate limit and later reversed, per DefiLlama's hack record. Young low-fee venues carry smart-contract and accounting risk that fee comparisons ignore. (low confidence) — https://defillama.com/protocol/arcus-perps
- [statement] GRVT's rate limits count by main account ID (shared across all sub-accounts) and include requests made via WebSocket, such as JSON-RPC calls. Writes per (/10sec) at every tier: Create 260 (tracked separately for every trading pair), Cancel 2600 and CancelAll 2600 (tracked across all trading pairs), and 1 for Transfer or Withdraw. Reads scale with tier: GetOrder from 50 at tier 1 to 650 at tier 9, and All Others from 25 to 225. Market-data REST allows 1500 per minute for GetInstrument, MiniTicker and Ticker and 500 per minute for all others. The MM program lists a Rate Limit Increase as a Diamond-category benefit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/9636566-what-are-the-rate-limitations-on-grvt · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/13606302-grvt-mm-program
- [statement] GRVT's API-key login returns a session cookie (gravity=...) in the Set-Cookie response header and your X-Grvt-Account-Id in the response headers, and an API-key session expires after 1 day (web browser session 7 days, mobile app session 90 days). The default whitelist limit is 5 IPs per API key, and an IPv6 address must be whitelisted separately. GRVT APIs cannot be accessed from IP addresses located in the United States, United Kingdom, or China, even with a valid API key and a whitelisted IP. Cloudflare's bot-fight protection can block API calls from certain server IPs (particularly AWS datacenter IPs). A key set to Read Only or Transfer Only cannot be used to trade, and RPI orders require the sub-account to be whitelisted by GRVT. Hummingbot's page names the Trading ID (sub_account_id in the GRVT API docs) as a required credential, and the GRVT Python SDK repo has a commit adding OrderWithBuilderFee EIP-712 signing support. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://help.grvt.io/en/articles/14117414-how-to-troubleshoot-authentication-errors-when-using-the-grvt-api · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://hummingbot.org/exchanges/grvt/, https://github.com/gravity-technologies/grvt-pysdk

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A third-party estimate (Alea Research, cited by Bankless) puts Variational's Q3 spreads at 2.35 basis points (bps) of volume versus 2.40 bps in average perp fees on Hyperliquid, suggesting zero fees on Variational are not hiding a worse deal. This is an estimate partly built on the team's own disclosures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public
- [statement] Aster's API limits are tracked per IP (the header X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT shows request weight used by your IP) and the order rate limit is counted against each account (X-MBX-ORDER-COUNT header). Breaching a limit returns HTTP 429, ignoring 429s triggers an automated IP ban (HTTP 418) that scales in duration from 2 minutes to 3 days, and HTTP 503 means the execution status is UNKNOWN rather than a failure. The docs recommend WebSocket streams over REST polling. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md
- [statement] EdgeX's V2 API has public endpoints (metadata, quotes, funding; no authentication required) and private REST and WebSocket endpoints that need a signature-based authentication mechanism, plus an EIP-712 Layer 2 signature for trading operations. Official Python and Go SDKs exist, production REST is at https://edgex-prod-v2.edgex.exchange and WebSocket at wss://edgex-quote-prod-v2.edgex.exchange, and the docs note SDK coverage may differ from the full platform endpoint set. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/api-v2 · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/edgex-Tech/edgex-python-sdk
- [statement] Nado's gateway rate limits are weight-based: IP addresses have a max weight limit of 2400 per minute or 400 every 10 seconds applied only to queries, wallet addresses 600 per minute or 100 every 10 seconds applied only to executes, and users can have up to 500 open orders per subaccount per market. Placing orders without spot leverage is limited to 30 per minute or 5 every 10 seconds because those orders are 20x more expensive to place, versus 600 per minute with spot leverage. The sequencer is described as striking the orderbook at 5-15 ms latency with settlement via the Ink L2. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.nado.xyz/developer-resources/api/rate-limits · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.nado.xyz/, https://nadohq.github.io/nado-python-sdk/index.html, https://github.com/ccxt/ccxt/tree/master/python/ccxt
- [statement] Several venues expose a machine-readable fee query, so a bot can read effective rates at startup instead of hard-coding them: Aster GET /fapi/v1/commissionRate (HMAC SHA256), Extended GET /api/v1/user/fees, Decibel GET /api/v1/user_fee_rates, Nado's Fee Rates query (IP weight = 2), Hibachi's public exchange-info response (a feeConfig object with tradeMakerFeeRate and tradeTakerFeeRate), Arcus GET /v1/markets/feeSchedules, and EdgeX contract metadata (defaultMakerFeeRate and defaultTakerFeeRate per contract). Arcus' docs state rates can change without a release. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://api.docs.extended.exchange/, https://docs.decibel.trade/for-traders/fees, https://docs.nado.xyz/developer-resources/api/rate-limits, https://data-api.hibachi.xyz/market/exchange-info
- [statement] Aster's V3 futures API documents two per-minute limiters in exchangeInfo: REQUEST_WEIGHT with a limit of 2400 and ORDERS with a limit of 1200, and the order rate limit is counted against each account. Breaking a limit returns HTTP 429, and continuing to send after 429s triggers an automated IP ban (HTTP 418) whose length scales from 2 minutes to 3 days. The docs advise reading order status and position updates from the WebSocket user data stream rather than REST endpoints, because REST responses can be delayed during extreme market volatility. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs
- [statement] EdgeX's V2 docs describe public APIs (market data, metadata and funding rates, no authentication required), private APIs (account management, order operations, asset management and transfers, authentication required) and WebSocket APIs, and warn that SDK coverage may differ from the full platform endpoint set. The edgex-Tech Python SDK repository shows 26 Commits and a latest commit 'Bump version to 2.0.1'. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://edgex-1.gitbook.io/edgeX-documentation/api-v2 · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/edgex-Tech/edgex-python-sdk
- [statement] Alea Research (2026) calculated that Variational traders paid $26.8M of spread in Q3 on $114.2B of volume, with the spread at 2.35 bps of volume versus 2.40 bps of average perp fees on Hyperliquid; the treasury took in $5.36M, which is 20% of every spread. Spread per dollar fell from 2.81 bps in August to 2.09 bps in September and 1.64 bps over Oct 1 to 14 as swaps took a larger share of volume. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://alearesearch.io/newsletters/variational-climbs-to-fourth · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.variational.io/omni/the-omni-liquidity-provider-olp, https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public
- [statement] A zero-fee RFQ quote is not always the cheapest. Alea Research's median round-trip cost of a $1M trade before fees (median of six snapshots on Oct 8, 2026) was, for trade.xyz's order book versus Variational's quote: Nasdaq 100, 2.04 and 0.88 bps; S&P 500, 2.40 and 1.87; gold, 4.57 and 3.63; Brent crude, 11.47 and 9.80; silver, 6.64 and 10.18; WTI crude, 6.94 and 11.92. Variational quoted lower on the Nasdaq 100, the S&P 500, gold and Brent; trade.xyz on silver and WTI crude. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) — https://alearesearch.io/newsletters/variational-climbs-to-fourth
- [statement] Bullet offers post-only variants: its order types are Limit (GTC), Fill or Kill (FOK), Immediate or Cancel (IOC), Post Only, Post-Only Slide and Post-Only Front. In the API, PostOnly is rejected if it would immediately match, PostOnlySlide slides to the best non-crossing price instead of rejecting, and PostOnlyFront posts at the front of the queue at the best price that doesn’t cross; orders also take reduce_only, client_order_id and an attached take-profit / stop-loss pair. Time In Force and TWAP are listed as Coming Soon. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.bullet.xyz/exchange/trading/order-types-and-tp-sl.md · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://tradingapi.bullet.xyz/docs/order-fields.html

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Aster's API docs recommend V3 for all new integrations. New V1 API key creation is no longer supported from March 25, 2026 (existing keys keep working). From September 1, 2026, 00:00 UTC, authenticated Spot V3 / Futures V3 endpoints are only accessible after the main wallet linked to the Aster account has completed a deposit; until then affected requests return code -5050 'This function can only be used after deposit'. Agent Wallet, Builder and public market-data endpoints are unaffected. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17) — https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.asterdex.com/for-developers/aster-api/api-documentation
- [statement] GRVT API access uses an API key plus secp256k1 private key signing; the Secret Private Key is shown only once at key creation. Hummingbot published a bot-development guide for GRVT, so third-party bot tooling exists. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://hummingbot.org/blog/trading-on-grvt-with-hummingbot-a-complete-bot-development-guide/
- [statement] Bankless reported that Variational planned a trading API: on Nov. 4th a team member said the API would go to a small group of alpha testers ahead of a public launch this month. The launch is not confirmed in the sources read. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12) — https://www.bankless.com/read/variationals-broker-bet-goes-public · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://docs.variational.io/technical-documentation/api
- [statement] Since September 1, 2026, 00:00 UTC, authenticated Aster Spot V3 / Futures V3 endpoints (account, order, trade and other USER_DATA / TRADE endpoints) only work after the main wallet linked to the Aster account has completed a deposit; until then affected requests return code -5050 'This function can only be used after deposit'. Agent Wallet, Builder and public market-data endpoints are unaffected. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://github.com/asterdex/api-docs · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asterdex/api-docs/master/V3(Recommended)/EN/aster-finance-futures-api-v3.md
- [statement] Extended's API uses an X-Api-Key header for API access and, for write operations (order management, transfers, withdrawals), also requires a Stark signature generated with the account's private Stark key under the SNIP12 standard (EIP712 for Starknet); you can create up to ten sub-accounts per wallet address, each with its own API and Stark keys. Order placement is asynchronous: an order ID returns immediately, before the order is recorded in the book, and status is tracked on the Order WebSocket stream. REST is throttled per IP at a default of 1,000 requests/minute (Tier 1 4,000 on request, Tier 2 8,000 above $50M and Tier 3 12,000 above $150M of 30-day trading volume), a 429 status code is returned on excess, the User-Agent header is required, and the exchange servers are hosted in the AWS Tokyo region (AZ ap-northeast-1a). The Python SDK is at x10xchange/python_sdk. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.docs.extended.exchange/ · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/x10xchange/python_sdk
- [statement] Extended's fee endpoint response example includes a builderFeeRate field (example value 0.0001) next to makerFeeRate and takerFeeRate, and the endpoint accepts a builderId parameter; the docs also list builder dashboard and builder trades endpoints. Check builderFeeRate before sizing a strategy through a third-party builder integration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api.docs.extended.exchange/
- [statement] GRVT supports API authentication via session cookies, API keys, and wallet login (EIP-712); it lists CCXT (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, PHP, and C#) as an integration path; its services are hosted in AWS Tokyo (ap-northeast-1), with AWS PrivateLink offered to close partners with high trading volumes. A Hummingbot bounty (#8046, sponsored by GRVT) was opened to add a GRVT Perpetual connector. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api-docs.grvt.io/ · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://github.com/hummingbot/hummingbot/issues/8046, https://hummingbot.org/blog/trading-on-grvt-with-hummingbot-a-complete-bot-development-guide/
- [statement] Hibachi's API key is required for almost all endpoints except /market REST and /ws/market WS endpoints, and it is not used for signing: trustless accounts sign with an ECDSA private key and exchange-managed accounts (created via email or social login) sign with an HMAC secret key. API keys default to read-only permission (read-write is selectable), the Account ID is not generated until the first deposit (USDT or USDC on Arbitrum One, or USDC on Base Mainnet), and an official Python SDK (hibachi-xyz 0.3.2) is on PyPI. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://api-doc.hibachi.xyz/ · keywords: Other zero or near-zero fee perp DEXs · also: https://pypi.org/project/hibachi-xyz/
- [statement] StandX's perps HTTP API (https://perps.standx.com) requires JWT authentication for all endpoints except public endpoints, with a token validity of 7 days, plus signed bodies (x-request-sign-version, x-request-id, x-request-timestamp and x-request-signature headers) for trading calls. A successful response only indicates the order was submitted, and some orders, such as ALO orders, may be rejected during matching, so execution status should be read from the Order Response Stream using a consistent x-session-id. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22) — https://docs.standx.com/standx-api/perps-http
